news.headline: Dispute over parking, dog ended in ex-Tech Mahindra executive's murder in Faridabad; neighbour arrested
news.story_lead: Dispute over parking, dog ended in ex-Tech Mahindra executive's murder in Faridabad; neighbour arrested The victim had arrived in India from Singapore on November 5 to celebrate Diwali with his family and was also scheduled to attend his nephew's wedding. A dispute over parking space and a dog in Faridabad's Sector 21C turned fatal on Friday night when the former regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region was shot dead by his neighbour. The accused, who fled after opening fire at the victim, was arrested later.
news.full_article_text: Dispute over parking, dog ended in ex-Tech Mahindra executive's murder in Faridabad; neighbour arrested The victim had arrived in India from Singapore on November 5 to celebrate Diwali with his family and was also scheduled to attend his nephew's wedding. A dispute over parking space and a dog in Faridabad's Sector 21C turned fatal on Friday night when the former regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region was shot dead by his neighbour. The accused, who fled after opening fire at the victim, was arrested later. Paramjith Dhankhar, who had returned from Singapore just a day earlier to celebrate Diwali with his family, was shot dead by his neighbour Mohan Sharma after an argument over parking escalated. Sharma allegedly fired 15 rounds, nine of which hit Dhankhar. Parking, dog dispute between neighbours Tensions between the two families had been mounting over Sharma’s dog defecating in the parking area. This prompted repeated objections from Dhankhar’s family. The disagreement had led to several confrontations over the past few days, including an argument four to five days before the shooting. An argument broke out between Dhankhar and Sharma again on Friday night over car parking. Following this, Sharma allegedly called Dhankhar out of his house and shot him multiple times with his licensed pistol. Accused arrested from Ballabgarh Sharma had allegedly fled with his family following the fatal shooting. However, he was later arrested from Ballabgarh in Faridabad, police said. “The suspect is being quizzed and will be produced before a Faridabad court and taken on police-remand for detailed interrogation,” Faridabad ACP (crime) Varun Kumar Dahiya said. As reported by HT earlier , Dhankhar, was settled in Singapore and was working as the senior vice-president of a software company. He had arrived in India from Singapore on November 5 to celebrate Diwali with his family. He was also scheduled to attend his nephew’s wedding on November 24. news.full_article_text: - Published 7 November 2026, 17:48 GMT At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city. Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car". Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard. - Follow live updates from Krakow A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured. People run for shelter as gunshots heard in Krakow Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the attacker, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said. The gunman was shot but is alive and has been arrested. Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times. The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself. Moment police officer appears to shoot Krakow suspect Shop windows in the square have signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor. City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues. The suspect's car, found at the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, is being checked for possible explosive devices, police say. Residents of nearby buildings are being evacuated while the operation is under way. How many people have died and been injured? Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed, including a British national. Three victims are Polish and two have not been identified. Sixteen people, including five foreigners and the attacker, were taken to hospital. Among those being treated are two police officers who were shot while detaining the attacker. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk later said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack. One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added. Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims. What do we know about the suspect and motive? Police have identified the attacker as a 25-year-old Polish man but have not confirmed his name. The suspect was wearing "military-style attire" and had a military-grade weapon, according to a police spokesperson. However, authorities have confirmed the attacker was not a soldier. "Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle", the spokesperson added. Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home. A minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details. His home is being searched with support from counter-terrorism police. How did witnesses describe the attack? The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination. Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started. Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down. "A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises." Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend. She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice". Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is on his way to Krakow and is expected to give an address later on Saturday. Earlier, he said he was being kept informed by the interior minister and that police were investigating "the background and all the circumstances". Krakow Mayor Åukasz GibaÅa has signed an order declaring a period of mourning in the city which will last until Wednesday, November 11. President Karol Nawrocki said he was "deeply concerned" and was awaiting "a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these tragic events". US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose described it as a "savage and murderous attack". The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland". news.headline: Reserve Bank of India Dismisses Viral Claims Regarding New Cheque Book Rules Implementation
news.story_lead: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has clarified that viral reports claiming the introduction of new cheque book rules starting from January are fake. The central bank dismissed these unverified claims circulating on social media to prevent confusion among bank account holders. Banking customers are advised to rely strictly on official communications issued by the RBI.

### RBI Clarification on Cheque Book Rules

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued a clarification dismissing claims circulating regarding the implementation of new cheque book rules starting in January. The central bank categorized these reports as fake, reassuring banking customers and account holders that no such changes have been mandated by the regulator.

**Key Factual Details:**
* **Official Stance:** The Reserve Bank of India confirmed that rumors regarding new cheque book regulations taking effect from January are false.
* **Public Advisory:** Customers are urged to verify banking rules and policy updates directly through official RBI press releases and verified communication channels rather than unverified social media messages.
bullet_points: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has labeled claims of new cheque book rules taking effect in January as fake.
Reports circulating regarding modified cheque book guidelines were clarified to be false.
The central regulator advised bank customers not to fall for unverified rumors on social media.
Official guidelines or regulatory updates are communicated directly through RBI's official channels.

The central bank issued a public clarification regarding viral rumors.
